name: Executive order of December 20, 1881 setting apart the Vermilion Lake reserve for the Bois Forte Band
nations: Bois Forte Band of Chippewa (Nett Lake), Minnesota Chippewa Tribe
promises: This was an executive order, not a treaty. The President set apart a reserve at Vermilion Lake: part of the southeast quarter of section 23 east of Sucker Bay, the southwest quarter and the southernmost lot of section 24, fractional sections 25 and 26, and the part of section 35 north of Vermilion Lake, all in T. 62 N., R. 16 W., Minnesota (Royce area 629).
landTaken: None by this order: it set land apart (Royce area 629).
today: The Bois Forte Band's Indian Claims Commission case (Docket 18-D) concerned the 1866 treaty cession of Royce area 482 and its consideration, not this reserve; in 1977 the Commission disallowed most of the government's claimed treaty payments, including buildings put up several miles outside the Bois Forte Reservation. That finding belongs to the 1866 treaty record (kappler-924).
